messages:
sasha: T-minus 90m — final preflight for the EU midweek cold deploy. Quick status check + explicit rollback triggers. Canary target: errors < 0.1% and p95 < 1.2s. Speak now or we proceed.
marc: +1. I recommend starting at 10% canary weight then 10m ramp to 30%. Keeps blast radius small.
kevin: heads-up: last-minute index migration landed in staging, not prod. It’s a low-risk read-index change but fyi in case we need a hold.
anya: I’d prefer to hold if we can’t verify migration roll-forward within the next 60m. Docs change can wait. :thinking_face:
sasha: understood — plan A is proceed with canary, plan B (hold) if migration verification fails in 60m. Anyone object?
marc: no objection. If we need to hold, we should pin current binary and model version to avoid drift.
deploy-bot: canary job queued: canary-id=eu-mid-cold-2026-03-21-01. Starting at 10% traffic to edge pool eu-west-1. Logs streaming to https://logs.redwood/ci/canary/eu-mid-cold-2026-03-21-01
ops-bot: thermal alert policy active for eu-west-1 GPUs — temp threshold 85C. Will notify if sustained > 80C for 3m.
kevin: quick check — are we pinning model version or letting runtime pick latest compatible variant?
sasha: pin model to v1.4.3-dec19 for this rollout. Runtime fallback policy enabled to v1.4.2 only if v1.4.3 fails health checks.
anya: for rollback triggers please use: errors > 5% sustained for 10m OR p95 latency > 2x baseline for 5m OR any critical customer error spikes. Add manual abort channel: #release-hotline.
sasha: agreed. Documented rollback command (if needed):
```
# roll back to last pinned binary + model
scripts/rollback_release --to=stable-20260310 --model=v1.4.2 --reason="canary spike"
```
marc: noted. Also logging: enable verbose traces for canary only (no perf cost for prod).
deploy-bot: canary started: 10% -> health checks OK (uptime 99.99%, errors 0.03%, p95=760ms) — 5m window in progress.
kevin: running quick migration verification against a sampled shard. ETA 18m. Will post result here.
anya: if migration check is green in 60m we lift the contingency and continue ramp. If not, we pause and pin current release — call @sasha to make final hold.
(small pause, deploy-bot messages follow)
deploy-bot: canary 10% after 10m: errors 0.04% (20 requests), p95 780ms, cpu 45% on workers. No error patterns.
sasha: good. Start scheduled ramp to 30% now. Keep alerting thresholds same.
deploy-bot: ramping to 30% now — canary weight change applied.
ops-bot: observed one brief GPU temp bump to 82C for 90s on eu-west-1a, cooled under threshold. Logging note created.
kevin: migration verification: sampled reads look consistent, no missing rows; I'm marking migration as VERIFIED.
anya: ACK. With verification we’re clear to keep ramping per plan.
sasha: final checklist: 1) Pin v1.4.3 model ✅ 2) Canary started ✅ 3) Migration verified ✅ 4) Rollback triggers set ✅ 5) Channel #release-hotline monitored ✅ — proceeding to 60% in 10m.
marc: pro tip: watch the reranking endpoint — it’s the most volatile on cold start.
deploy-bot: canary 30% after 10m: errors 0.06% (35 requests), p95 920ms, successful health checks. No sign of regressions.
sasha: great. I’ll post release notes draft in #eng-releases-later and start the quiet-window countdown. If anything breaches the rollback criteria we hit the command above and regroup. :rotating_light:
anya: thanks — I’ll keep an eye on error budgets and readiness dashboard.
marc: :thumbsup: Ready to abort if we see correlated spikes.
ops-bot: alert watchers after 60m will escalate to paging policy if error rate >1% for 5m.
deploy-bot: canary 60% scheduled in 10m. Current metrics stable.
sasha: closing preflight — go/no-go = GO unless automated triggers fire. Posting the final go note to the release ticket. Thanks all.
